fatal_blockers: None of the six proposals supplies a complete fixed CVP basis, target, weights, matched satisfiable control, coefficient bound, and exact shell threshold. Therefore their claims of avoiding G1-G6 and supporting unrestricted search are not currently verifiable.

Proposal 1 uses linear gain equations, so an affine combination of complete honest encodings remains zero-residual; incompatible cycle products only constrain deviations not already in this affine image. The known G13 coefficients are constant, directly defeating the claimed coefficient growth, so rerunning them on an unspecified gain graph is not discriminating.

Proposal 2 specifies neither the Lawrence matrix nor a finite search space for its entries, ranks, targets, or harmful fibers. A constant-size Graver-basis computation would not establish a polynomial-size family, composition law, or dimension-dependent norm gap, and G13 remains a candidate constant conformal move.

Proposal 3 does not define the claimed 2-complex, stalks, restrictions, target class, or expander cover; the variable-clause incidence object alone is only a graph. Linear sheaf boundaries preserve affine combinations, so G13/G15 can yield a trivial target class or constant-support representative unless an explicit construction proves otherwise.

Proposal 4 fails the Generation-29 reopening conditions: no exact seed Gram, integer two-copy lattice, target, matched control, coefficient bound, shell radius, or acceptance ratio is frozen. Coordinates representing v tensor v are nonlinear in CVP coefficients; making them independent reintroduces unrestricted non-rank-one pseudotensors, while symmetric projections do not enforce rank one.

Proposal 5 provides no explicit polynomial-size concatenation or exact Gram/target. Delsarte bounds on code distances do not control arbitrary signed integer combinations, and a fixed local frame leaves G13 or a clause drop at constant excess relative to a growing honest baseline; a nine-clause scheme search cannot resolve this scaling defect.

Proposal 6 cannot linearly enforce matroid independence or common-base membership inside CVP. If it instead enforces common column sums, every compatible assignment of matroid columns preserves the G13 affine relation as a short exact dependence; no explicit representation, target, objective, or finite lift enumeration is supplied.
evidence: Generation 13 verifies that the harmful parity selector is an exact integral affine combination of 16 honest encodings and annihilates every compatible linear syndrome tested; Generation 15 lifts the same coefficients through an enlarged hierarchy with zero residual.

Generations 7 and 11 exhibit constant-cost exact kernels, while Generation 12 shows that charging a parity kernel can expose a cheaper clause drop. These directly contradict residual-only or single-attack geometric amplification.
Generation 19 finds an exact accepting signed flow with two negative coefficients, confirming that finite-state or linearized nonlinear semantics remain vulnerable to unrestricted splicing.

Generation 14 supplies only a finite pair-bag shell pass, and Generation 28 then measures adverse growth below legal growth. Thus finite local separation does not provide the composition law claimed by the toric, tensor, coding, or matroid proposals.
No verifier evidence is supplied for any Generation-30 construction, and no proposal establishes a uniform polynomial-size family or an asymptotic gap.
